key_insight: A data-free weak-form staggered neural operator can learn coupled finite-strain magneto-mechanical responses directly from physics, without labeled finite-element training data.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast surrogate modeling for magneto-active elastomers across changing microstructure, geometry, and material contrast, reducing the cost of coupled multiphysics design and analysis.
method: Enforce magnetostatic and mechanical governing equations through finite-element weak-form residuals.
Train separate magnetic and mechanical neural operators in an alternating staggered scheme.
Use the learned operator to initialize a nonlinear Newton finite-element solve.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across heterogeneous random-inclusion microstructures, varying phase contrast, area-fraction-dependent geometries, strongly out-of-distribution morphologies, and 3D geometry-parametric problems.
watch_item: Because the approach relies on weak-form physics residuals and staggered coupling, performance may depend on residual weighting, solver stability, and how well the chosen parameterization spans unseen morphologies.
paper_title: Data-Free Weak-Form Staggered Neural Operators for Magneto-Mechanical Coupling in Finite-Strain Elastomers
